title: San Lazaro Hospital reports downward trend in leptospirosis admissions

blocks.text: Leptospirosis admissions at San Lazaro Hospital are on a downward trend, with the daily count dropping to four on Monday, Sept. 7. The hospital recorded its highest daily admission count at 50 on Aug. 26, after which admissions declined before rising again to 40 on Sept. 3. The number then dropped to 23 on Sept. 5, 13 on Sept. 6, and four on Sept. 7. More patients were also discharged than admitted over the past two days, with 32 patients discharged on Sept. 6 and 34 on Sept. 7. Monitoring continues following the Aug. 17 and 29 flooding in Metro Manila brought by the southwest monsoon or “habagat,” which may have exposed residents to contaminated floodwaters. Leptospirosis is associated with exposure to water or soil contaminated with the urine of infected animals. San Lazaro Hospital advised the public to avoid wading in floodwaters and to wash with clean water and soap after possible exposure. People are also advised to keep their surroundings clean and free from rodents, drink safe water, and eat well-cooked food. Those exposed to contaminated floodwaters should watch for symptoms such as fever, headache, muscle pain, and jaundice and seek immediate medical attention if they develop them.
